properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 declared in the lockfile: ships SHA-1/SHA-224/SHA-256/SHA-384/SHA-512 implementations as a transitive dependency (via elliptic@6.6.1 and the browserify/Ethereum-JS stack). This is the dependency inventory — the package ships with the build; no direct hash.js import exists in the app's own modules (index/main/swap/fuc/grpc/parsingtransaction).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@4.2.0 declared in the lockfile; bundles MD4/MD5/SHA-1/SHA-2/HMAC/PBKDF2/Escalade modules. Presence in the shipped build is what this entry records; no direct crypto-js import found in the app's own modules. Changeable here by dropping the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@4.2.0's SHA-1 module, same lockfile entry as ALG-70109388. Ships with the build; no direct crypto-js call site in the app source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile dependency inventory for all three Node bots: bcrypt-pbkdf 1.0.2 (the OpenSSH bcrypt KDF, transitive via sshpk/http-signature chain) plus the nested tweetnacl 0.14.5 entry at :4042; line 8935 is the same family in the third lockfile. No direct app call site (the bots take keys from env, not passwords), but it ships with the installed tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 native addon (ECDSA over secp256k1) declared as a dependency edge and installed entry in all three bots' lockfiles — pulled by the Ethereum-JS stack. Ships with the build. Solana itself does not use secp256k1 for transaction signing (that is Ed25519); this rides in via the Ethereum-side packages.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.9.7 declared in the lockfile; provides secp256k1 ECDSA among its curve implementations, pulled transitively via the Ethereum/anchor stack. Ships with the build; no @noble/curves import in the app's own modules.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/ed25519 1.7.5 in all three lockfiles (dependency of metaplex-foundation and irys packages). Ed25519 is also the live signature scheme of every Solana transaction these bots sign — the actual signing call sites (Keypair.fromSecretKey → transaction.sign in each project's swap.js) are being reported as separate findings since no roster site covers them.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (at least Node.js 16.0.0)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves 1.9.7 resolved in the lockfile provides Ed25519 (plus secp256k1/P-256) to the Solana/anchor dependency tree of all three bots. Distinct from ALG-5e08bdf5 (the @noble/ed25519 standalone package) — different packages providing the same algorithm family.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.6.1 declared in the lockfile; ECDSA over secp256k1/P-256 is its primary primitive, a transitive dependency of the Ethereum-JS stack. Ships with the build; no elliptic import in the app's own modules. The library-level facet of this same dependency is LIB-a0bfbc1a.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.9.7 also provides P-256 (secp256r1) ECDSA/ECDH. Same lockfile entry as ALG-92b28f71, different curve facet. Ships with the build; no call site in the app source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.6.1 also exposes ECDH key agreement (elliptic.ecdh / derive). API surface of a shipped library — the package is in the build via the Ethereum-JS stack, but no ECDH call site exists in the app's own modules.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 pinned in the lockfile as @solana/web3.js's signer (web3.js uses its Ed25519 crypto_sign); X25519 (crypto_scalarmult/crypto_box) is part of tweetnacl's shipped API. tweetnacl is also declared directly in package.json (^1.0.3). Available in the shipped library; no X25519 call site found in the application source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 ^3.0.9 npm package (28 entries across the three lockfiles — e.g. dependency of the bip39-light/browserify chain at package-lock.json:4119). PBKDF2 capability ships in the installed tree; no app-level PBKDF2 call site found in the bots' own code (they load raw secret keys from env).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 hashing ships with the build via the Ethereum stack: @ethersproject/keccak256 ^5.8.0 (dependency edges at multiple packages) and the native keccak ^3.0.2 module, declared identically in all three bots' lockfiles. No keccak import in this bot's own modules; presence recorded.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 declared in the lockfiles — the memory-hard KDF used by the Ethereum BIP39/mnemonic stack; transitive dependency identical in all three bots. No scrypt call site in the app's own modules; presence in the shipped build is what this records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Rust bot's AES-256-GCM helper: Aes256Gcm::new(key) in encrypt_data (:35) and decrypt_data (:63) of solana_helper.rs; 32-byte key from ENCRYPTION_KEY env var (hex), 12-byte OsRng nonce, output base64(nonce||ciphertext). Caveat: solana_helper.rs is not declared in src/lib.rs and aes-gcm is absent from Cargo.toml [dependencies] — the module is dead code in this snapshot (won't compile as-is), but it is real crypto code on disk.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl's crypto_secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305 AEAD) ships in the build via @solana/web3.js's tweetnacl pin. Available in the shipped library; no secretbox call site found in the application source. The app's observed tweetnacl use is Ed25519 transaction signing (reported separately).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl ^1.0.3 is a DIRECT dependency of all three bots (package.json dependencies) and is the signing engine inside @solana/web3.js Keypair — Ed25519 signatures and XSalsa20-Poly1305 box/seal. Live use: Keypair.fromSecretKey → transaction.sign in each bot's swap.js (reported as findings). The "." site is the tree-level detection; the package-lock site is the resolved declaration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The crypto provider for the Rust sniper: openssl = { version = "0.10", features = ["vendored"] } (Cargo.toml:29) compiles vendored OpenSSL into the binary; it backs reqwest's native-tls transport used for the Jito/NextBlock block-engine HTTPS submissions (src/core/tx.rs:159/:181). Whether the binary can offer PQ TLS at all is decided by this vendored OpenSSL version.
